title: Leading PowerShell call operator silently prevents focused Node verification recognition
outcome: A single native test/build invocation using PowerShell's leading call operator receives a truthful host-recognition result without weakening compound-command or source/provenance guards; supported forms can produce recognized verification, and unsupported forms explain why no record follows.
acceptance: A deterministic regression captures the leading PowerShell call-operator command reported by Codex and the observed absence of a host verification despite a valid native Node14 PASS artifact; the fix either recognizes the safe single invocation or explicitly reports the unsupported form with no fabricated credit.

Tests preserve rejection of actual compound commands, unquoted control operators beyond a permitted leading call operator, substitutions, malformed argv, foreign or stale artifacts, and missing native execution; ordinary recognized Node/cargo commands keep their existing behavior.
The exact final input has the maintained full gate, independent review pair and independent acceptance required by project policy.
